gappers.catalyst_detail: No same-day company-specific negative catalyst exists. AMKR is giving back part of Monday's move: on 2026-11-23 the entire AI/semi complex ripped higher (Nasdaq-100 futures +882 pts / +3.5%; AMKR itself closed +15.1% off Friday's $30.21 low at $34.77, and OSAT peer ASX ran ~+20%). This morning the same complex is reversing in unison. The only genuine AMKR news is a token ~1% quarterly dividend raise ($0.08352 -> $0.08436) approved around 11-20/11-21, which is a positive, not the cause of a -5.5% gap. The standing fundamental overhang is the 2026-10-26 Q3 print: revenue $1.99B flat YoY and 245bps below consensus, with forward revenue and EPS guidance narrowed below consensus, driven by a multi-year smartphone upgrade-cycle slowdown (mobile is ~45% of revenue; Verizon and other carriers are pulling back from handset subsidies, VZ Q3 upgrades -20%).
gappers.why: Pure sector beta, not an idiosyncratic move. A peer sweep at an 08:09 ET read shows the whole complex gapping down together: MU -6.15%, FORM -5.59%, AMKR -5.49%, TER -5.25%, CRWV -4.76%, NVDA -4.70%, KLIC -4.26%, STM -4.07%, AMD -3.97%, NBIS -3.89%, GFS -3.72%, ASX -3.58%, QCOM -2.47%, TSM -1.80%. AMKR sits mid-pack in a ranked list of its own peers, which is the signature of index/basket de-risking rather than a stock-specific event. As a high-beta, 9.3%-ATR OSAT name it simply amplifies the group: it overshot on Monday's squeeze and is overshooting on the unwind.
gappers.impact: Reads as continuation of a two-day whipsaw, not a fresh directional move, and is the opposite of sustainable in either direction. AMKR is $32.90 against SMA20 $35.98, SMA50 $43.50 and SMA200 $56.14 - below all three, roughly 66% off the 52-week high of $96.53 and only ~10% above the 52-week low of $29.95 set on 11-20. RSI(14) is 45.5, i.e. neutral, so there is no oversold-bounce edge either; the Monday rally burned off the oversold condition without repairing any moving average. ATR(14) is $3.05, 9.3% of price, so a -5.5% gap is well inside one day's normal range and carries little information. Sector read-through is total: this is the same AI-infrastructure de-rating that has been driving the watchlist for weeks (CRWV and NBIS are gapping with it), so the signal to take from today is a regime read on the whole book, not a trade in AMKR.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The gap itself is headline-free sector beta inside a two-day mean-reversion whipsaw and should be expected to keep chopping, so there is no durable thesis to carry. The underlying AI advanced-packaging story (~$3B NVIDIA commitments, $12B Arizona OSAT build, computing+auto/industrial now 48% of revenue, +1,100bps YoY, margins expanding with net income +50% on flat revenue) is genuinely LONG_TERM and fits the Technology leg of the sector-rotation table, but management has guided below consensus and the sell-side case itself puts the real reversal in 2027 when top-line growth resumes. A structural story whose own timeline is next year is not a gap trade today.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing is displaced: the account is flat at $100,000 cash, 0 of 6 position slots used and 0 of 3 weekly trades spent, so the true cost is optionality rather than an existing holding. It also would not displace a better name from today's list, because today's list has no other qualifying name (WLDS was the only other hit and fails the $3 price floor). The binding objection is the rulebook, not the opportunity set: price is below the 200-SMA, so the long-bias filter in TRADING-STRATEGY.md fails outright, and the Confluence rule cannot reach 2-of-4 with RSI neutral at 45.5, price below all three MAs and no insider signal. On R:R, ATR 9.3% means a sane stop sits ~10% out at ~$29.61, which is *below* the 52-week low of $29.95 - i.e. the only technically sane stop is already through support - and clearing 2:1 would need ~+20% to ~$39.48, above SMA20 and into SMA50 resistance, requiring the entire sector to reverse to pay. Fails the Entry Checklist on catalyst, trend filter and R:R simultaneously. The real value of today's scan is the regime read, which argues for preserving the dry powder and the 3 unspent weekly trades rather than spending one catching a falling knife in the weakest sector on the tape.
